Tautomerism:
• For keto–enol tautomerism a carbonyl group must possess at least one α-hydrogen on an sp³–hybridised carbon.  
• Cyclohexane-1,3,5-trione has three C=O groups each flanked by CH₂ carbons; it can enolise and even tautomerise to the aromatic phloroglucinol form, so it does show tautomerism.  
• In 1,4-benzoquinone the carbons α to the carbonyls are vinylic (sp²) and bear no α-hydrogen that can be shifted. Hence ordinary keto–enol tautomerism is impossible.  
Therefore the compound that does NOT show tautomerism is benzoquinone.

Optical isomerism:
• Methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate (methyl lactate, CH₃–CH(OH)–COOCH₃) has the CH-carbon bonded to four different groups (H, CH₃, OH, COOCH₃). It is a chiral centre and the molecule exists as a pair of enantiomers – it is optically active.  
• Dimethyl fumarate (the trans ester of fumaric acid) has a plane of symmetry and no chiral centre; despite having E/Z (geometrical) isomerism potential, it cannot show optical isomerism.  
Hence the compound that shows optical isomerism is methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate.

Combining the two conclusions:
A = benzoquinone (does not tautomerise)  
B = methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate (shows optical isomerism)

Answer: B
